title: Attribution & deterministic sampling for inference KPIs (OTel + Prometheus convergence)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Inconsistent attribution and high-cardinality blowup for our inference KPIs across OTel and Prometheus consumers. We currently emit per-request labels that include model_variant, route, and user_agent leading to metric cardinality spikes and skewed p99 latency calculations. Goal: produce a deterministic, low-cardinality attribution schema and an adaptive sampling strategy so Prometheus and downstream analytics see stable, comparable KPIs for latency, error-rate, and token-throughput.
scope: 1) Define canonical KPI labels and cardinality budgets (model_family, model_variant_tag, route_id, client_tier). 2) Implement deterministic sampling at the trace/span level using consistent hashing on request_id to ensure sampled traces proportionally represent traffic segments. 3) Add server-side aggregation hooks that emit pre-aggregated buckets for Prometheus (latency_histogram_by_route/model) while still sending detailed OTel traces for sampled requests. 4) Update exporters and the ingestion pipeline to respect sample flags and attribution mapping. 5) Dashboard updates and validation queries in Grafana/BigQuery.
deliverables:
- Specification doc with attribute whitelist and cardinality budgets (link in attachments).
- OTel SDK change: deterministic sampler module + tests.
- Exporter changes: Prometheus pre-aggregation counters and histograms with reduced label set.
- Migration script to normalize existing metric names and labels.
- Dashboard updates for p50/p95/p99 by model_variant_tag and route_id.
- Load test results showing <5% additional error/noise at 5% sample rate.
acceptance_criteria: Prometheus metrics maintain cardinality <= defined budgets under 1M RPS test stand
p99 latency from Prometheus agrees within 3% of p99 computed from sampled OTel traces after bias correction
Deterministic sampler is stable across restarts (same request_id -> same sample decision)
No customer-facing labels (PII) are included in emitted metrics or traces
Dashboards reflect new canonical label names and are populated for last 7 days in staging
open_questions: What should the default sample rate be per customer tier? (suggestion: 1% free / 5% pro / 10% enterprise)
How do we surface sampling windows/flags in the Console so SREs can debug observed variance?
Do we keep a small tail-sampling buffer to capture anomalous long-lived requests?
implementation_notes:
- Deterministic sampling will use xxhash64(request_id) % 10000 < (rate*10000).
- Add a middleware hook in serving runtime to attach 'rw.sampled' tag to trace/span and expose it to exporters.
- Prometheus exporter will consume pre-aggregated telemetry emitted to a local push gateway endpoint to avoid high-cardinality label surfaces.
- Use label normalization table: model->model_family, variant->model_variant_tag, route->route_id. Map unknowns to 'unknown' token.
- Ensure metrics emitted for attribution are accompanied by a sampling_denominator gauge for bias correction in analytics.
- Add e2e test in infra/bench with Faker traffic across 200 model variants to validate cardinality constraints.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable sampler and reduced labels for 5% of staging traffic; wire dashboards to new metrics. Phase 2 (canary): rollout to 10% of production traffic for select customers with telemetry. Phase 3: full rollout with migration script renaming legacy labels and backfill windows. Keep dual-writing for 14 days to allow downstream queries to transition.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: sampling bias causing under/over-estimation of tail latency. Mitigation: bias-correction using sampling_denominator and run offline replay to validate. Risk: missed critical low-volume customers if sampling deterministically drops them. Mitigation: exempt customers with <X RPS or enable targeted sampling override via route labels.
